newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Canada sets 3rd round of specials at 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank Canada sets 3rd round of specials at 3.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Thursday conducted a third round of special purchase and resale agreements in the money markets at 3.5 percent.
The central bank intervened on the money markets after the call loan or overnight lending rate traded continued to trade at the top of the central bank's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
Dealers said the rise in the call loan rate is linked to month end and quarter end pressures, as well as normal settlement pressures from the weekly T-bill tender on Tuesday.

"The system starting out this morning was so dislocated. I think some of the major banks were scrambling to get covered," said one T-bill trader with a Canadian bank. "I think what you're seeing is an equilibrium taking place. Don't read anything into it."
The call loan rate continued to trade at 3.5 percent in the wake of the third round of specials. The three-month when-issued T-bill traded to yield 3.29 percent.
